## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` `bbe57fdd52bf69f993decba179a64dfc89b26e97`

The card was filed `2026-09-14T00:12Z` against a future state — *"once it lands"*. It has landed, so the asymmetry is live on `main` today, ⛔ not pending:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| PR objectui#9343 | **merged** `2026-09-14T03:59:49Z` |
| the `detail` arm's by-name refusals | present — `packages/types/src/zod/crud.zod.ts:205` `onNavigate`, `:222` `onAddComment` |
| `onNavigate` in `packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` (the `detail-view` arm) | **0** |
| `onAddComment` in the same file | **0** |
| **lit control** `onBack`, same file | **3** |
| **lit control** `handlerKeyRefusal`, same file | **2** |
| **absent-token control** | **0** |

⇒ the same two keys have two different fates depending on which `type` literal an author wrote. Confirmed.

## ⚠️ The census the card did NOT run, started here and NOT finished — it decides whether this is dispatchable as a mechanical repair

A by-name refusal **narrows what a published JSON authoring face accepts**. Whether that breaks anybody is a measurement, and this seat took the first cut only:

| probe over `content/docs/**`, `examples/**`, `*.json`, `*.mdx` | files |
|---|---|
| `onNavigate` | **4** |
| `onAddComment` | **2** |
| `onBack` | 2 |
| **lit control** `detail-view`, same corpora | **3** |
| **absent-token control** | **0** |

⛔ **Those are not yet an answer.** A hit is only a break if the key sits **on a `detail-view` node**; a hit on a `detail` node, on some other node type, or in prose is not. ⇒ the order requires the implementer to refine this to node-level and to **STOP and report** if any authored `detail-view` node carries either key — at that point it stops being a mechanical repair and becomes a breaking-change question for the maintainer, ⛔ not the dev's and ⛔ not this seat's.

## Clause-② — declared **no**, with the reasoning, and a STOP if it is wrong

The `detail-view` zod arm **declares neither key**; today's acceptance is an accident of `BaseSchemaCore`'s `.passthrough()`, ⛔ not a declaration. Adding `handlerKeyRefusal` makes the arm say explicitly what its member list already implies, and brings it into line with its own twin. That is 「拉回已声明契约」, which this board has ruled is ⛔ not clause ② — the triage seat wrote exactly that on objectui#8236's thread, and the lane charter says narrowing stays 语义面.

⇒ `Clause-②: no`, ⛔ no carrier hung. ⚠️ The order requires a STOP if the repair turns out to widen anything or to need a name on a published barrel — that flips the declaration and is ⛔ not the dev's to decide. Per the lane charter, declaring `yes` is never an error, so if the implementer's own reading disagrees it should say so and this seat will hang the carrier.

## ⛔ Attributed and still not measured — the card says so and this seat did not close it either

*"`detail-view` feeds the **same** `DetailView` component through `DetailViewRenderer`'s derived `bound` object, which is why `scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` cannot see the read."* ⇒ the implementer re-derives that path first: it decides whether the fix is 「mirror the refusal onto `detail-view`」 or something narrower.

## File face, declared

`packages/types/src/zod/views.zod.ts` · `packages/types/src/views.ts` · new pins · changeset.

Checked against all **12** open PRs plus this seat's two other in-flight cards (objectui#9692 / PR objectui#9697, objectui#8236 dispatched in the same act): **zero intersection**.

## ACCEPT — the STOP did not fire, the fence held, and the carrier the implementer asked for is filed

Each of the 12 is accounted for: two are this diff's own new files, two are the TS face and the twin arm (`views.ts`, `crud.zod.ts`), one is the gate script, the rest are ledgers, docs and prose |

⚠️ **The implementer reported the intersection as 9 files and this seat's instrument reads 12.** ⛔ Neither is wrong: it measured at base `bbe57fdd5`, this seat measured at the head, and the diff itself adds two of the three extra files. Recorded rather than smoothed, for the same reason as the test-count divergence on objectui#9692 earlier today — **two different instruments quoted as one number is how a figure starts to drift.**

## The gating measurement: the STOP did not fire

The dispatch attached a STOP — *if any authored `detail-view` node carries either key, do not repair; report and this becomes a maintainer question.* The implementer refined this seat's file-level cut to **node level** and it came back negative: **zero authored `detail-view` nodes carry either key as a member.** The classifications that matter, in its words: the `schema-reference` hits sit under the `DetailSchema` heading (the twin arm's own prose); `DetailView.test.tsx`'s five `onNavigate` keys are **all nested under `recordNavigation`** (indent 8 against node keys at 6), a different key with a different signature, in a suite that renders the component directly and never parses; `examples/` contributes **zero**; and neither first-party producer writes either key (`record-details.tsx` 0/0, `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` 0/0) against lit controls `objectName` 15/14 and `sections` 17/0.

⇒ the repair proceeds, and the narrowing breaks nobody.

## The read path — the thing the card admitted it had never measured

The card said outright that it did not re-derive this and that it **decides the repair**. The implementer did, and its finding is sharper than the card's framing: `detail` registers `DetailView` **raw** while `detail-view` registers a **wrapper**, `DetailViewRenderer` — so a wrapper really is in the path, but it **does not strip the key**. `useElementDataSourceSchema` has exactly two branches: return the node unchanged, or a shallow spread whose only overwrites are the binding keys. `DetailView` then reads `schema.onNavigate` and **calls** it, and forwards `schema.onAddComment` into `RecordComments`, which awaits it. The new 13-test pin drives both to their call sites rather than asserting them.

⭐ And the implementer separated the card's *mechanism* from the card's *fact* rather than adopting either: it took the fact from a run and flagged the mechanism as its own reading. That is the discipline this board keeps failing at, done right.

## Clause-② — `no`, and this seat concurs

Re-derived independently by the implementer, which reports all three STOP conditions negative: nothing widens; no name is added to a published barrel (`DetailViewSchema` is already exported from `@object-ui/types/zod` — the diff adds two **members** to an already-exported object); and the TS face does not move. ⇒ ⛔ no at-tier contract review is owed and ⛔ no `needs:contract-review` carrier is hung.

## The 11 pending changesets — answered, all still true

The `changeset-claim-re-read` gate flagged 11 pending declarations naming files this diff edits. This seat sent the ask mid-round; the implementer answered all 11 **by paragraph** and returned **zero corrections**, so ⛔ no pending body was touched and no frontmatter question arises. The probes worth naming: the objectui#7344 **STOP check is negative** (`onViewChange` 3 at base and 3 at head, `onChange` 6 and 6, all three still `z.string().optional()` — it did not touch the three keys that entry declares untouched); the objectui#6150 / objectui#7804 containment claims measured directly (`RuntimeOnlyDeclared`'s **entry** set identical at base and head, entries outside `UnmirroredDeclared` = 0, union = 14 = `UnmirroredDeclared`'s 14 — **no entry moved, only keys inside one surviving entry**); and the `UnmirroredDeclared` and `EXCLUSIONS` blocks hash byte-identically at base and head, with the same extractor firing on a ledger the diff **did** edit, so the instrument is lit rather than merely silent.

⭐ **The implementer reported a probe of its own that was wrong first time and kept both readings.** Its initial `EXCLUSIONS` check used a crude 400-lines-after-first-mention window, which spans regions this diff edits, and reported a false difference; extracting the actual `const EXCLUSIONS` block gives byte-identical hashes. It reported both rather than deleting the wrong one. That is the correct handling of a broken instrument and it is worth more than the result.

## The carrier the implementer asked for — filed as **objectui#9700**

Its one open request. `scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` **exited 0 on a tree carrying a live instance of exactly what it hunts** — this card's own instance. Re-measured by this seat before filing, on `origin/main` `bbe57fdd5`: an exemption row `detail-view::` reads **0** in that file, beside a **lit control** `detail::` at **2** and an **absent-token control** at **0** ⇒ the reads were **neither found nor exempted**. And the gate's own docblock publishes the capability that failed — 「imports, **transitively**, with a visited set」, 「**The transitive hop is not a flourish: it is the shape of the very instance**」 — with a `hops > 4` cap in `resolveComponent`, so the following is real and bounded by design. ⇒ declared ≠ enforced.

⛔ The card states the **mechanism as unmeasured** and says so twice, because the outcome is all that was measured. ⚠️ `detail-view` is one instance; the class (`kanban`, `calendar`, `gantt`, related-list and any other wrapper-registered arm) is ⛔ **unmeasured** and the card claims no population — the sweep was fenced out of this round on purpose.

The implementer's three other out-of-scope findings are correctly dispositioned and this seat adds nothing: `onTabChange` already has objectui#7804 as its carrier and stays ledgered; the dated 2026-07 audit is left alone on the right ground (**a dated audit is evidence about its own moment; editing it destroys the signal instead of reading it**) with 「承接者:无」 stated rather than a carrier invented; and the stale `onBack` parenthetical was repaired in passing as a same-file opportunistic fix, which AGENTS.md permits and a sweep would not.

## ⛔ Enqueue is HELD — CI is not green yet

Read on head `baae0f389` at `2026-09-17T15:16Z`: **36 returned = 36 `total_count`** ⇒ complete enumeration; **28 success / 3 skipped / 0 failures**, and **5 still running** — `Test (shard 1/4)` through `(4/4)` and `Type Check`. `Lint`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs` and `Changeset Declaration` are already green.

⛔ Zero failures is not a green reading while five required jobs are in flight.

⚠️ `mergeable_state` reads **`behind`** — `main` moved to `82edae063` while the implementer worked. It correctly left that alone: the merge queue rebuilds on current `main`, and this seat confirmed that path today when PR objectui#9697 enqueued and merged from a base that had moved under it. ⛔ Not a blocker, and ⛔ not a reason to push a sync commit.

Then: ready → enqueue, confirmed **positively by the queue ref** against the ~12,600-ref lit control — ⛔ never the `auto_merge` field, and ⚠️ **giving the ref time**: this seat measured today that a probe fired ~6 seconds after a successful enqueue reads a **false zero**, because the ref is not created synchronously.
